name: OpenTelemetry GenAI Tracing
question: Where did this run go wrong?
summary: A trace records one request as a tree of spans: the agent invocation, every model call and every tool call, with timings, token counts, model versions and errors. The OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions, still in Development status, standardise the span and attribute names, so any compatible backend can read them. When quality drops, traces let you group failures by any attribute and find what they share.
useCases: Any agent in production: you cannot fix what you cannot see
Incidents where the cause could be the model, a tool, a prompt or the data
Cost and latency questions: tokens and time per step, per user, per release

items.detail: prompts and outputs are not captured by default; opt in and redact personal data

steps: Set up an OpenTelemetry tracer provider and an OTLP exporter to your backend
Open one root span per request, with child spans for each model and tool call
Record the response model, token usage, finish reason and errors on each span
Query traces grouped by attribute when a metric moves
pitfalls: Logging only the requested model hides a silent provider-side change
Capturing full prompts can store customer personal data in your tracing backend
Sampling away errors: keep every failed trace, sample the successful ones
remember: One span per step. Record what was served, not just what was asked.
caption: Illustrative incident: the provider moved an alias to a new snapshot overnight. Only gen_ai.response.model separates the failures.

comparison.scope: Why a run failed, which step, which version

code.text: def run_agent(claim_id: str, text: str) -> str:
def call_tool(name: str, arg: str) -> str:
def call_model(text: str, policy: str) -> str:
# In the backend: failure rate grouped by gen_ai.response.model

steps.title: Set up the tracer
steps.text: A tracer provider batches spans and exports them over OTLP to any compatible backend: Jaeger, Grafana Tempo, Langfuse, Phoenix or a vendor. Your code only talks to the OpenTelemetry API.

steps.title: Open a root span per request
steps.text: Each claim gets one invoke_agent span. Every later span nests under it, so the whole run reads as one tree, and the conversation id ties it to the claim.

steps.title: Wrap each model call
steps.text: A chat span carries the two required attributes, gen_ai.operation.name and gen_ai.provider.name, plus the model you asked for. The span name follows the convention: operation, then model.

steps.title: Record what was served
steps.text: After the call, record the model that actually answered and the token counts. Here the request said alpha-latest, but the response says alpha-0918: the provider moved the alias.

steps.title: Wrap each tool call
steps.text: An execute_tool span names the tool. If it throws, the exception and an ERROR status go on the span, so failures are searchable rather than buried in logs.

steps.title: Group failures by attribute
steps.text: When success drops, group failed traces by each attribute in turn. Prompt, tool and region split evenly; gen_ai.response.model does not: 94% on the old snapshot, 84% on the new one.

pros: Turns “it got worse” into a query over evidence
Per-step timings, tokens and costs for every run
Auto-instrumentation covers common SDKs with little code
cons: The GenAI conventions are still in Development, so names can change
Storage and backend costs grow with traffic
Content capture creates a privacy and retention burden
Custom agent steps still need manual spans
avoidWhen: A prototype with a handful of users, where printed logs are enough for now
Capturing full prompts and outputs of regulated data without redaction and access controls

playgroundGuide.scenario: An Indian general insurer’s claims copilot summarises health claims for the claims desk. At 02:00 the share of summaries accepted without edits fell from 94% to 86%, and nobody deployed anything. You are on call. Decide what your spans record, group the failed traces by an attribute to find what they share, and choose a fix.
controls: Choose whether spans record only the requested model or the full GenAI attributes, including the model that actually served each call.
Group the failed traces by prompt version, tool, region or gen_ai.response.model, and look for a group that differs.
Pick a fix, or load a scenario to see a blind guess and a traced diagnosis side by side.

outputs.name: Grouped by
outputs.meaning: The attribute used to split the traces, with the success rate and traffic share of each group.

outputs.name: Cause found
outputs.meaning: Whether the grouping isolates the failures, which needs the response model on the spans.

outputs.name: Success now
outputs.meaning: Share of summaries accepted after the chosen fix.

outputs.name: Time to recovery
outputs.meaning: 12 minutes to alert, plus diagnosis (8 min with evidence, about an hour without), plus the fix.

presets.name: Plain logs, no grouping
presets.expect: Success 86%, cause not found, not recovered.

presets.name: Guess: group by region, restart pods
presets.expect: Every region sits near 86%; the restart changes nothing, so success stays at 86%.

presets.name: Full attributes, grouped by response model
presets.expect: alpha-0712 at 94% on 20% of traffic, alpha-0918 at 84% on 80%: cause found, no fix yet.

presets.name: Found and pinned
presets.expect: Pinning alpha-0712 restores 94%; recovery takes 25 min (12 + 8 + 5).

library.name: OpenTelemetry Python SDK + GenAI instrumentation
library.what: Vendor-neutral tracing. The opentelemetry-instrumentation-openai-v2 package emits GenAI spans for OpenAI calls automatically; you add spans for your own agent and tools.

practice.note: Auto-instrumentation records gen_ai.request.model and gen_ai.response.model for you. Query your backend for failure rate grouped by gen_ai.response.model when quality moves.

samples.code:
import os
from opentelemetry import trace
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import BatchSpanProcessor
from opentelemetry.exporter.otlp.proto.http.trace_exporter import OTLPSpanExporter
from opentelemetry.instrumentation.openai_v2 import OpenAIInstrumentor
from openai import OpenAI

# Opt in to the latest (still experimental) GenAI conventions; keep content capture off.
os.environ.setdefault("OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN", "gen_ai_latest_experimental")

provider = TracerProvider()
provider.add_span_processor(BatchSpanProcessor(OTLPSpanExporter()))  # OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT
trace.set_tracer_provider(provider)
OpenAIInstrumentor().instrument()              # emits a "chat {model}" span per call

tracer = trace.get_tracer("claims-copilot")
client = OpenAI()

def summarise(claim_id: str, text: str) -> str:
    with tracer.start_as_current_span("invoke_agent claims-copilot") as span:
        span.set_attribute("gen_ai.operation.name", "invoke_agent")
        span.set_attribute("gen_ai.agent.name", "claims-copilot")
        span.set_attribute("gen_ai.conversation.id", claim_id)
        span.set_attribute("app.release", "cfg-7f3a")       # your own release id
        r = client.chat.completions.create(model="gpt-4o-2024-08-06",
                                           messages=[{"role": "user", "content": text}])
        return r.choices[0].message.content

numericDrill.question: A root span lasts 4.2 s. Its child spans run one after another: a chat span of 1.6 s, a tool span of 0.5 s and a second chat span of 1.7 s. How many seconds of the root span are not covered by any child span?
numericDrill.answer: The children cover 1.6 + 0.5 + 1.7 = 3.8 s, so 4.2 − 3.8 = 0.4 s is spent in your own code between calls: parsing, validation or queueing. That gap is worth a span of its own if it grows.

interview.question: Why record gen_ai.response.model as well as gen_ai.request.model?
interview.answer: The request says what you asked for; the response says which snapshot actually served it. When you call an alias, the provider can change the snapshot behind it, and only the response attribute reveals that. Grouping failures by it is often the fastest route to the cause of an overnight drop.

interview.question: Should you capture full prompts and completions in traces?
interview.answer: Not by default. They can contain customer personal data, and the GenAI conventions leave content capture off unless you opt in. Capture content only where you need it, redact personal data first, restrict access, and keep metadata such as tokens, models and errors on every span.

mistakes.mistake: Logging one line per request with no step structure
mistakes.fix: Emit a span per model call and tool call under one root span

mistakes.mistake: Sampling traces uniformly, so rare errors disappear
mistakes.fix: Keep every error trace and sample the successful ones

quiz.question: A claims copilot’s success rate fell 8 points overnight with no deploy. Spans record only the model name sent in the request, the alias alpha-latest. Which attribute would most directly reveal a provider-side model change?
quiz.explanation: The response model is the snapshot that actually served the call; the request only shows the alias you asked for.

quiz.question: A bank is adopting the OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions for its loan assistant. Which pair of attributes is required on a chat span?
quiz.explanation: Operation and provider are required; model and token attributes are recommended, and message content is opt-in.

quiz.question: Following the GenAI span naming convention, what should a chat call to a model named beta-2 be called?
quiz.explanation: Chat spans are named by operation then model: “chat {model}”. invoke_agent names the agent’s root span.

quiz.question: An order-support agent’s root span lasts 5.0 s. Its children run one after another: a chat span of 1.8 s, a tool span of 0.4 s and a chat span of 2.1 s. How much of the root span is not covered by child spans?
quiz.explanation: 1.8 + 0.4 + 2.1 = 4.3 s, so 5.0 − 4.3 = 0.7 s is spent outside the recorded calls.

quiz.question: A returns agent is being instrumented. Which should be recorded on every model span by default? Select all that apply.
options: The model that served the call
The full prompt, including the customer’s address
The whole conversation history as one attribute
quiz.explanation: Tokens and the served model are cheap and essential. Prompt content can hold personal data and stays off unless you opt in with redaction.

quiz.question: A hospital’s discharge-summary agent handles patient notes. The team wants traces for debugging. What is the best default for message content?
options: Capture all prompts and outputs, since the backend is internal
Put the prompt text into span names for easy search
Keep content capture off, record metadata, and enable redacted content only where needed
Do not trace this agent at all
quiz.explanation: Metadata such as models, tokens, timings and errors gives most of the debugging value without storing patient data.

quiz.question: A telecom support agent produces 2 million traces a day, and storing them all is too expensive. Which sampling policy keeps the most diagnostic value?
options: Keep every error trace and a sample of successful ones
Keep 1% of all traces, chosen uniformly
Keep only traces from the first hour of each day
quiz.explanation: Errors are rare and the most useful for diagnosis, so keep them all and sample the successful majority.

quiz.question: A delivery agent’s failures are grouped by attribute. By served model: every group is near 90%. By tool: get_eta traces succeed 61%, all others 93%. What is the most likely cause?
options: The get_eta tool or the API behind it
quiz.explanation: Only the tool dimension splits the failures, which points at get_eta, not at the model.

quiz.question: A rebooking agent’s seat-hold tool throws an exception. What should its execute_tool span record so the failure is searchable?
options: Nothing; the stack trace in stdout is enough
A new root span for the error
The exception, plus an ERROR status on the span
The exception text in the span name
quiz.explanation: Recording the exception and setting the status makes failed tool calls filterable in any trace backend.

quiz.question: A span records 3,000 input and 500 output tokens. Input costs $3 and output $15 per million tokens. What does this call cost?
Traces show success grouped by served model: alpha-0712 at 94% on 20% of traffic and alpha-0918 at 84% on 80%. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Rolling back the prompt is the most likely fix
quiz.explanation: 0.2 × 94 + 0.8 × 84 = 86%. The split is by served model, so pinning the old snapshot fixes it; prompt and region are not implicated.

quiz.question: A KYC agent’s trace shows a root span but no child spans, so nobody can tell which step is slow. What is missing?
options: Spans around each model call and tool call, nested under the root
quiz.explanation: Without child spans the trace has no step structure; each model and tool call needs its own span.

quiz.question: Why use the standard gen_ai.* attribute names instead of inventing your own, such as llm_model?
options: They are required for the model to work
Any compatible backend and tool can read and chart them without custom mapping
quiz.explanation: Standard names are what make traces portable across backends and dashboards.

quiz.question: A bank wants to see where tokens go in its dispute agent. Which trace-based analyses help? Select all that apply.
options: Sum input and output tokens per span name
Compare tokens per step across releases
Count spans per trace to find loops
Read only the final answer text
quiz.explanation: Token attributes per span show which steps cost most, how releases change that, and whether runs loop; the final answer alone shows none of it.

quiz.question: The OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions are in which status as of 2026?
options: Development, so names can still change
Only a draft proposal with no implementations
quiz.explanation: They are widely implemented but still in Development, which is why instrumentations offer an opt-in for the latest version.

quiz.question: An agent calls a moving alias. The same request model appears on every span for months. What does that tell you about the snapshot that served each call?
options: Nothing: only the response model shows the served snapshot
That the provider pinned it for you
quiz.explanation: The request carries the alias name every time, whichever snapshot the provider actually used.

quiz.question: An on-call engineer must find the cause of a quality drop quickly. Which trace attributes are worth grouping by first? Select all that apply.
quiz.explanation: Model and release are the usual suspects for sudden drops; timestamps and random ids do not form meaningful groups.

quiz.question: A payments agent’s p95 latency doubled. Traces show chat spans unchanged but execute_tool fraud_score spans went from 0.3 s to 2.4 s. Where should the fix start?
options: The fraud_score tool or its API
quiz.explanation: The step whose duration changed is the tool call, so that is where the latency comes from.

quiz.question: A team exports spans synchronously after each model call, and request latency rose by 40 ms. What is the usual fix?
options: Use a batch span processor that exports in the background
Put all attributes in the span name
quiz.explanation: A batch processor queues spans and exports them off the request path.

quiz.question: A health-tech firm must trace an agent handling patient queries under India’s data protection rules. Which practices fit? Select all that apply.
options: Redact personal data before any content is stored
Restrict access to traces that contain content
Keep traces with content forever for convenience
Send full prompts to a third-party backend by default
quiz.explanation: Redaction and access control limit exposure; unlimited retention and default content export increase it.
